newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia seen shutting out Sinn Fein leader - paper.
newsitem.headline: Australia seen shutting out Sinn Fein leader - paper.

text.p: Canberra is expected to refuse an entry visa to Gerry Adams, leader of Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army (IRA), The Australian newspaper reported on Saturday.
It said Adams had asked to enter Australia later this month to promote his autobiography.

The Australian cabinet was to discuss his application on Monday but key government departments, including the foreign affairs department, were opposed to it because of the breakdown of the Northern Ireland ceasefire, it added.
"The government is strongly of the view it must exclude anyone who explicity or implicitly endorses political violence or terrorism," the newspaper said.
Asked about the report, a spokesman for Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said he could not comment on what the cabinet would discuss nor confirm that Adams had applied for a visa.
He said all visa applications were judged on their merits and the government had a long-time policy on visa applications by Sinn Fein leaders, which had to meet certain conditions.
"It would depend on the state of play of the ceasefire and what his attitude to it was," spokesman Peter Collins told Reuters.
The Australian said that senior government members were concerned that Adams had not condemned the IRA's resumption of violence after the February 9 ceasefire breakdown.
The IRA ended the 17-month truce by attacking British targets in Britain and Germany, then struck in Northern Ireland last month with an attack on Britain's army headquarters.

Britain and Ireland, partners in an attempt to forge a lasting political settlement to 27 years of Northern Ireland conflict, say Sinn Fein cannot be invited to peace talks until there is a new IRA truce.
Sinn Fein says the talks are designed to make IRA guerrillas surrender their weapons, and it refuses to accept this as a precondition.
